newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia three-month KLIBOR fixed at 11.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia three-month KLIBOR fixed at 11.3 pct.

text.p: Malaysia's benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) was fixed at 11.3 percent at 0300 GMT.
It was at 14.9 percent on Monday.
The one-month KLIBOR was fixed at 12.85 percent against 17.5 percent on Monday.
KLIBOR is fixed by taking an average of rates offered by various banks in the country.
Money market dealers said the fall in interbank rates came after lending of one-month and overnight funds by agent banks of Bank Negara on Monday.

Dealers said Bank Negara was believed to be lending to ease the market which was short of ringgit funds following the central bank's heavy buying of the currency last week to defend the ringgit from a speculative attack.
Although the actual size of the intervention was not known, dealers were estimating between 2.5 billion and 5.0 billion ringgit went out of the system.
"This suggest that focus has shifted to reducing interest rates to avoid the pitfalls associated with it," said research house MMS International in its market commentary.
Dealers said rates also came off ahead of maturity of Bank Negara bills worth 500 million ringgit on Wednesday.
One-week money was at 13/15 percent, against 25 percent on Monday.
The overnight rate is expected to remain at 8-10 percent, dealers said.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange rose across the board to reflect falling interbank rates.
At 0300 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up nine points to 92.41, or an implied yield of 7.59 percent.
The December contract rose eight to 92.65, or 7.35 percent.
